title: oncall-capability-matrix-and-rapid-handoff-procedure-2026
author: Jordan M. Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines a capability-based on-call matrix, a rapid handoff procedure for live incidents, and reusable artifacts (checklists, templates, and training curriculum) to reduce time-to-stable during high-severity events. It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, SRE leads, and engineering managers.

Scope:

- Applies to Redwood Inference services in the hosted, dedicated and private deployment fleets.
- Covers incident severities Sev1 (outage), Sev2 (partial outage/high-error-rate), and Sev3 (degraded performance/quality).
- Does not replace individual service runbooks; it complements them with people/process-focused handoff and capability guidance.

Owner and maintenance:

- Document owner: Jordan M. Patel (SRE Platform)
- Review cadence: quarterly; update after any game day or Sev1 postmortem
- Primary reviewers: SRE, Runtime, Customer Success

1) Incident responder capability matrix

A concise skills matrix describing expected competencies for on-call roles and recommended certification/training. Use this to staff rotations and match handoff responsibilities.

| Role | Core responsibilities | Minimum skills | Training / validation | Escalation target |
|------|-----------------------|----------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| First Responder | Triage, initial evidence capture, engage bridge | Logging/metrics queries, basic kubectl/gcloud, runbook navigation | 1x tabletop + shadowing (2 runs) | Escalate to Bridge Operator in 10–15m if not contained |
| Bridge Operator | Run bridge, coordinate cross-team actions, customer comms | Bridge tooling, status page updates, incident timeline creation | Bridge simulator + 1 live supervised handoff | Escalate to Incident Lead after 30m if multiple services implicated |
| Incident Lead | Decision authority, runbook orchestration, severity adjudication | Prior postmortem authoring, RCA techniques, service dependency map | 2x game days + 1 live lead with mentor | Engage Leadership & Customer Success in 45–60m for Sev1 |
| Subject Matter Expert (SME) | Deep-fix implementation and verification | Codebase, model-serving internals, perf tooling, KV cache inspection | Certification by team lead (knowledge test) | N/A |

Skill levels are expected to be met at hiring or ramped within the first 60 days of rotation. Use the skill matrix in hiring and promotion conversations.

2) Rapid handoff procedure (5-minute handoff standard)

Goal: transfer operational context between responders with <5 minutes of interruption to the incident runloop. This reduces duplicate work and avoids stale assumptions.

Pre-handoff constraints:
- Make the handoff only at an atomic checkpoint (e.g., containment achieved, mitigation applied, failed workaround acknowledged).
- If the system is actively degrading and the outgoing responder cannot finish the checkpoint, escalate immediately and do not perform a partial handoff.

Rapid handoff checklist (step-by-step):
1. Prepare (outgoing responder): gather the following in the bridge chat or runbook page:
   - One-line status summary (current observable impact)
   - Severity level and time since detection
   - Top three hypotheses and evidence for/against each
   - Active mitigation steps and their status (commands run, signals toggled)
   - Pending actions and required permissions (e.g., need for deploy approval)
   - Key logs/trace links and metric graph links
2. Announce (outgoing): call out "Handoff-ready" in bridge, paste the one-line status and where full context lives.
3. Confirm (incoming): repeat back the one-line status and ask a single clarifying question if needed.
4. Transfer (both): outgoing stays in the bridge for two minutes while incoming performs a quick verification sequence (see Verification Commands).
5. Close (incoming): acknowledge ownership by posting the standardized ownership stamp (see Handoff Template).

Verification Commands (examples):
- kubectl get pods -n serving | grep -E "redwood-runtime|batcher"
- curl -sS "https://grafana.redwood.company/d/serving?panelId=1&from=now-15m&to=now" | sed -n '1,20p'
- redis-cli -h cache-host INFO replication

Handoff SLA: Ownership must be visible in the bridge roster and the runbook page within 2 minutes of the close step.

3) Standardized handoff template (paste into bridge chat & runbook)

Handoff Template (single message):

---
OWNERSHIP STAMP:
- New owner: @username
- Time: 2026-02-20T15:42Z
- Severity: Sev2
- One-line: "Partial tokenization failures in model-v2 causing 15% request errors in eu-west-1"
- Evidence: logs: https://log.redwood/abcd, grafana: https://grafana/redwood/serving/err-rate
- Active mitigations: rolled back canary to model-v1, prefix cache warmup in progress
- Next actions: (1) verify cache warmup completion (2) monitor residual error rate for 20m
---

Copy/paste this verbatim for every ownership change. The template creates a consistent incident timeline for post-incident analysis.

4) Severity-specific anchors and primary runbook locations

- Sev1 (Outage): follow "sev1-bridge-activation" runbook. Primary objective: Customer-visible restoration within SLA window. Escalate to Incident Lead and trigger executive notifications per Exec Notification SOP.
- Sev2 (High error rate / partial outage): follow "sev2-containment-and-mitigation" runbook. Primary objective: reduce user-impacting errors by 80% or meet acceptable workaround.
- Sev3 (Degradation): follow "sev3-degraded-performance" runbook. Focus on stabilizing load shedding, throttles, and quality fallbacks.

Runbook table (service anchors):

| Service | Primary runbook page | Runtime lead |
|---------|----------------------|---------------|
| Serving API | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/serving-api-sev1 | @luca.moretti |
| KV cache | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-containment | @simone.alvarez |
| Routing/Smart Router | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/routing-fallback | @rae.thompson |

5) Pre-bridge checklist (what the first responder must do before bridge handoff)

- Pin at least 2 independent telemetry links (logs + metrics) in the bridge chat.
- Capture the initial incident detection time and detection source (alert, customer, internal).
- Attempt one safe mitigation with rollback instructions documented.
- Notify Customer Success for customer-impacting Sev1s within 10 minutes.

6) Evidence collection requirements (for postmortem quality and SLO validation)

Every incident must collect the following artifacts and attach them to the incident page before handoff closure: 
- Full alert timeline (alert ids and timestamps)
- Representative logs w/ correlation ids (sanitized for PII)
- Grafana snapshots for key SLO panels (error rate, latency P50/P95/P99, request volume)
- Sampling of failing requests (request id, model version, hint)
- Commands executed with exact timestamps and who ran them

7) Game day syllabus and scoring rubric

Purpose: validate capability matrix, practice rapid handoffs, and exercise cross-team coordination. Run quarterly and after any major platform release.

Game day components:
- Scenario design: include model-quality regressions, KV cache stampedes, and cross-region capacity blips.
- Roles: designate First Responder, Bridge Operator, Incident Lead, SMEs, and Communication Liaison.
- Objectives: contain within 30m for Sev2 scenarios, full restoration within 60m for Sev1 scenarios (non-customer-impacting exercise can use simulated latency).

Scoring (pass/fail thresholds):
- Handoff speed: <5m (pass) / 5–15m (partial) / >15m (fail)
- Evidence completeness: all artifacts collected (pass) / missing 1–2 items (partial) / major gaps (fail)
- Customer comm accuracy: refer to status page template and timeline (pass if used correctly)

After-action: every game day requires a short retro, list of action items, and an update to the skill matrix if gaps are discovered.

8) Status page and customer communication templates

Use these minimal, templated messages for public status updates and targeted customer notices. Keep language simple, avoid technical speculation, and provide a clear ETA where possible.

Status page: initial incident notice (public)
- Title: Service Degradation - [region] - [short cause summary]
- Summary: We are investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation requests in [region]. Our engineers are investigating.
- Impact: Customers may experience increased errors or latency for generation and chat endpoints in [region].
- Start time: 2026-02-20 15:30 UTC
- Next update: 30 minutes

Customer-targeted notice (email / support portal)
Subject: Incident affecting text generation in [region] — initial update
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We are currently experiencing an incident affecting text generation requests in [region] which may cause increased errors or latency. Our engineering team is actively investigating and we have applied an initial mitigation. We will update you within 30 minutes or as the status changes.

If you rely on private deployments, please contact your Dedicated account lead for a scoped response.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support Team

9) Post-incident requirements and postmortem rubric

- Draft postmortem must be created within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2 and within 7 days for Sev3.
- Postmortem must include: timeline, root cause hypothesis and evidence, corrective actions (short and long term), owner for each action, and verification plan.
- Priority for action items: P0 (must ship before next deploy), P1 (next sprint), P2 (triaged into roadmap).

10) Rotation onboarding and shadow plan (first 8 weeks)

Week 0–1: Read the capability matrix, shadow two shifts as observer, complete bridge simulator course.
Week 2–4: First responder under supervision, complete evidence collection checklist twice.
Week 5–8: Bridge operator rotation (at least one shift with mentor), lead one non-customer-impacting game day scenario.

11) Escalation and contact matrix (quick reference)

- Bridge Operator: @bridge-ops on Slack / pager 1
- Incident Lead: @incident-lead on Slack / pager 2
- Security contact (if data incident suspected): security-oncall@redwood.company
- Customer Success escalation: cs-urgent@redwood.company

12) Ownership and document governance

- Document reviews scheduled quarterly.
- Major changes require sign-off from SRE Lead and Runtime Engineering manager.
- Failure to meet handoff SLA for two consecutive incidents triggers a remediation training for the responder.

Appendix A — Quick status page JSON (example)

{
  "id": "INC-20260220-1234",
  "title": "Service Degradation - eu-west-1 - Increased error rates",
  "status": "investigating",
  "impact": "partial",
  "start_time": "2026-02-20T15:30:00Z"
}

Appendix B — Sample postmortem checklist

- Create postmortem page and link to incident artifacts
- Assign owner and reviewers
- Populate timeline with timestamps and evidence links
- List corrective actions with owners and verification steps
- Publish and schedule follow-up verification meeting (30–90 days)

If you have questions about staffing, training, or the game day calendar, contact SRE Platform (sre-platform@redwood.company).
